KEY MESSAGE 1...
A very warm and humid Monday afternoon across the area with
temperatures ranging from the upper 70s in PA to the upper 80s
in Marion and dew points in the upper 60s and lower 70s. Low
impact weather is expected through Tuesday morning, though do
note it will be a muggy night with lows mainly staying up in the
lower to mid 70s with dew points only slightly cooler than that.
A weak shortwave glancing the region may continue to cause a few
light showers (and perhaps a stray storm) across the area
through early this evening before exiting east-southeast.
Another shortwave will glance the region late tonight/early
Tuesday, which will combine with ongoing warm air/moisture
advection to spark some showers and possibly an isolated storm
late tonight into early Tuesday. Any showers will exit to the
southeast by midday Tuesday. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...
Meteorological fall technically starts on Tuesday, but it will
not feel like it with a Heat Advisory in effect for a good chunk
of the forecast area. Upper ridging will reach peak amplitude
across the central and eastern U.S. Tuesday and Wednesday,
before shifting southwest as troughing builds over the Northeast
Thursday and Friday. A very warm and humid airmass (PWATs
climbing to nearly 2.00" and 850mb temperatures topping out at
20-22C) will support what is hopefully the season's last round 
of excessive heat across the local area through Thursday. 

High temperatures will range from the mid 80s to lower 90s on
Tuesday with dew points in the low to mid 70s. Wednesday appears
to be the hottest day, with highs ranging from the upper 80s to
mid 90s with dew points in the upper 60s and lower 70s. Thursday
will still be quite warm but trend a bit cooler farther north,
with highs forecast to range from the mid 80s to lower 90s with
dew points mainly in the lower 70s. There is some potential for
lingering cloud cover, afternoon convection, and a lake breeze
to keep far Northeast OH and Northwest PA slightly cooler on
Tuesday. Convection potential does add some uncertainty for
Wednesday and Thursday. Current consensus is that any lingering
convection will clear early Wednesday, with any renewed 
activity largely holding off until after peak heating. Thursday 
appears to have the greatest potential for convection to keep 
temperatures cooler than forecast. 

Arguments for the heat being hazardous/impactful include warm/
humid nights providing for limited relief, the multi-day 
duration, and some school buildings not having air conditioning 
across the area. So while forecast peak heat index values are 
on the lower end for a Heat Advisory and there is some 
uncertainty, opted for a Heat Advisory from the Cleveland- 
Akron area points west for Tuesday and Wednesday where 
confidence is overall the highest in peak heat index values 
nearing or reaching 100 degrees both days. We may need to expand
the advisory east to include more of our eastern Ohio counties 
for Wednesday, but these areas look a bit cooler on Tuesday than
areas farther west so left them out for now. Parts of the 
advisory may need to continue through Thursday, though 
uncertainty regarding the timing of the cold frontal passage and
convective potential are too high to do that yet. 

KEY MESSAGE 3...
The local area will be located on the edge of a heat ridge
through much of the week as a front waivers to our north through
Wednesday and pushes south Thursday and Friday. This will place
us in a potentially active corridor of weather for most of the
week, though overall confidence in the timing and location of
greater thunderstorm potential remains low. With that said, an
elevated mixed layer (EML) plume will lead to steeper mid-level
lapse rates atop very warm and humid low-levels, fueling
moderate to very strong instability across the area from Tuesday
afternoon until the cold front tries crossing Thursday into
Friday. West-northwest flow aloft will also be moderately
strong, providing sufficient shear for organized and potentially
severe convection. Precipitable water values climbing to 
1.70-2.00" in this very warm environment will also support 
torrential rain rates within convection and potential for heavy 
rain/flash flooding with any training or repeated rounds of 
convection through the week. 

Starting with Tuesday and Tuesday night, it's possible much of
the afternoon and evening hours are dry as there is a distinct
lack of large-scale forcing during that time. However, there's
good agreement in very strong and only weakly capped instability
developing Tuesday afternoon/evening. There may be some triggers
for afternoon/evening convection, mainly in the form of a lake
breeze near the northeastern lakeshore and potentially a
differential heating boundary left behind by morning clouds/ 
showers. These boundaries may support a few storms developing
during the afternoon or evening, mainly across northeastern
portions of our area. Greater potential for storms may arrive
